name: Honey & Mumford Learning Styles Questionnaire — short form (LSQ-40)
description: 40-item adaptation of Honey & Mumford's Learning Styles Questionnaire, derived from Kolb's experiential learning theory. Identifies four learning style preferences: Activist (learns by doing), Reflector (learns by observing), Theorist (learns by thinking), Pragmatist (learns by experimenting in real-world contexts). The original LSQ uses 80 items in agree/disagree form; this is a shortened Likert adaptation.
citation: Honey, P., & Mumford, A. (1986/2006). The Learning Styles Questionnaire. Peter Honey Publications. (Items written for this study based on the published Honey & Mumford behavioral descriptions; this is not the original LSQ-80.)
license: LSQ © Peter Honey Publications; items rewritten in Likert form for this study (CC-BY).

dimensions.label: Activist
dimensions.description: Enthusiastic about new experiences; learns by doing; thrives on challenge

dimensions.label: Reflector
dimensions.description: Cautious, thoughtful; learns by reviewing experiences; gathers data before deciding

dimensions.label: Theorist
dimensions.description: Logical, analytical; learns through models, principles, theories

dimensions.label: Pragmatist
dimensions.description: Practical, down-to-earth; learns by trying ideas in real situations

items.text: I enjoy throwing myself into new experiences without hesitation.
I like to take time to think things through carefully before acting.
I want to understand the underlying principles behind what I'm learning.
I'm most interested in ideas that have clear practical applications.
I get bored when situations don't offer enough variety or challenge.
I would rather observe a meeting first than dive into participating.
I'm uncomfortable with intuitive arguments that lack rigorous logic.
I get impatient with long, open-ended discussions that don't reach conclusions.
I make decisions quickly and tend to act on the first reasonable option.
I like to collect as much information as possible before deciding.
I prefer ideas to be presented in a clear, systematic framework.
I judge ideas by whether they actually work, not how elegant they are.
I'd rather be involved in something now than analyze it from the sidelines.
I like to consider all the angles before committing to a course of action.
I value rationality and logical analysis above feelings and intuition.
I prefer experts who can show me practical techniques over those who just theorize.
I'm drawn to lively, spontaneous, energetic activities.
I would rather listen to a wide range of perspectives than push my own view.
I want to know how ideas fit into the bigger conceptual picture.
I want to know the immediate practical benefit before investing time in something.
I'm willing to take risks and learn from what happens.
I prefer to revise and refine my views as new evidence comes in.
I find inconsistencies in arguments difficult to ignore.
I focus on what works rather than what 'should' work.
Open-ended group activities energize me.
I prefer to think carefully alone before sharing my conclusions.
I enjoy understanding complex systems and how their parts interconnect.
Theory bores me if I can't see how to apply it to something real.
I have a low tolerance for routine and repetition.
I rarely jump to conclusions without checking the evidence.
I am uncomfortable with vague concepts that haven't been precisely defined.
I like solving real problems more than discussing abstract ones.
I prefer trying new things to perfecting what I already know.
I am cautious and don't act until I've considered the implications.
I like ideas to be built on solid foundations of evidence and reasoning.
I'm at my best when I can take a tested technique and apply it to a new situation.
I'm happiest in fast-paced, demanding environments.
I'm a good listener and tend to draw out other people's thinking.
I prefer to learn within a structured curriculum rather than ad-hoc exploration.
I like learning from people who have actually done what they teach.
